$comment: scripts/fetch-bin.sh reads this file, downloads each input, verifies its sha256,
and assembles Sources/bin/<name>. Bumping a tool means editing this file only.
Every sha256 below is a real download checksum: for ipatool it matches the
sha256sum published next to the release asset, for go-ios (which publishes none)
it was computed from the downloaded zip.
archs lists what the *output* must contain; inputs are lipo'd when there is more
than one. No strip pass: it is only needed to squeeze the universal ipatool under
GitHub's 100MiB per-file limit, which stops applying once the binaries are not
committed - and strip(1) output is not byte-reproducible, while lipo is.
